Departementet gir nærmere forskrifter om klagenemndas organisasjon og saksbehand ling. Nytt kapittel XIV A skal lyde: Kap. XIV A. Om bindende forhåndsuttalel ser. § 58 A-I 1. Bindende forhåndsuttalelser i merverdi avgiftsspørsmål gis av Merverdiavgiftsnemn da. 2. Merverdiavgiftsnemnda har tre medlem mer som oppnevnes av departementet. Nemndas leder skal oppfylle de alminnelige krav til å være dommer. § 58A-2 1. En person, selskap eller innretning kan anmode om at Merverdiavgiftsnemnda gir bindende forhåndsuttalelse om de merverdi avgiftsrettslige virkninger av en konkret fore stående disposisjon før den gjennomføres, forutsatt at det er av vesentlig betydning å få klarlagt virkningene før gjennomføringen. 2. Merverdiavgiftsutvalget kan avvise an modningen uten å gi noen begrunnelse. En slik avgjørelse kan ikke påklages. 3. For anmodning som nevnt i nr. 1 betales et gebyr som for søksmål ved herreds- eller byrett, jfr. lov om rettsgebyr av 17. desember 1982 § 8. § 58A-3 En forhåndsuttalelse skal legges til grunn ved senere avgjørelser av merverdiavgifts spørsmål som gjelder samme person, selskap eller innretning, dersom vedkommende kre ver det og den faktiske gjennomføringen av disposisjonen er i samsvar med forutsetnin gene for uttalelsen. Forhåndsuttalelsen står li kevel tilbake for ny lovgivning. § 58A-4 1. Merverdiavgiftsnemndas forhåndsutta lelse kan påklages til Klagenemnda for mer verdiavgift av den som anmodet om uttalel sen og av Skattedirektoratet. Klagefristen er 14 dager. For øvrig kommer forvaltningslo vens kap. VI til anvendelse på slik klage. 2. Klagenemndas avgjørelse i saken kan bringes inn for domstolene etter de regler som gjelder om dette for avgjørelser i ordinæ re klagesaker. § 58A-5 1. Anmodningen om forhåndsuttalelse skal være skriftlig. Skattedirektoratet er adressat for anmodningen. 2. Merverdiavgiftsnemnda skal uten ugrun net opphold ta stilling til om anmodningen skal realitetsbehandles. 3. Realitetsbehandlingen av anmodningen finner sted i møte eller ved sirkulasjon etter lederens bestemmelse. 4. Realitetsbehandling skal skje innen 45 dager etter at anmodningen om forhåndsutta lelse ble mottatt av nemnda, forutsatt at sa ken er tilstrekkelig opplyst. Tilsvarende gjel der for behandling i Klagenemnda for mer verdiavgift etter § 58A-4. 5. Departementet kan gi nærmere forskrif ter til utfylling og gjennomføring av ordnin gen med bindende forhåndsuttalelse i mer verdiavgiftsspørsmål. Ny § 61 b skal lyde: Departementet kan ved søksmål få prøvet gyldigheten av vedtak i Klagenemnda for merverdiavgift. Slikt søksmål må være reist innen fire måneder etter at klagenemndas vedtak ble truffet. Søksmålet reises mot lede ren i Klagenemnda for merverdiavgift. Den avgiftspliktige skal varsles om søksmålet. Forliksmelding foretas ikke i sak etter denne paragraf. Ny § 68 a skal lyde: I særlige tilfeller kan det tilkjennes dekning av vesentlige sakskostnader som har vært nødvendige for å avklare rettstilstanden, på løpt før vedtak er fattet eller hvor vedtak ikke fattes. § 73 skal lyde: Den som forsettlig eller uaktsomt overtrer denne lov eller forskrifter gitt i medhold av lo ven, kan utover avgift fastsatt etter §§55 og 56, ilegges tilleggsavgift med inntil 100 pro sent av den avgift som derved er eller kunne ha vært unndratt staskassen. Fastsettelse kan foretas inntil 10 år etter utløpet av det kalen derår overtredelsen ble begått. Bestemmelse ne i § 56 gjelder tilsvarende. Bestemmelsen i første ledd gjelder også når det gis pålegg etter § 44 tredje ledd ominnbe taling av beløp som i salgsdokument er urik tig anført som avgift. Tilleggsavgift skal ikke ilegges hvis den av giftspliktige frivillig retter eller utfyller opp lysningene og innbetaler riktig avgift eller til bakebetaler for mye utbetalt overskytende beløp etter § 24. Første punktum gjelder ikke hvis rettingen kan anses fremkalt ved kon trolltiltak som er eller vil bli satt i verk eller ved opplysninger som avgiftsmyndighetene har eller kunne ha fått fra andre. Tilleggsavgift skal ikke ilegges hvor den av giftspliktige har avgått ved døden. For så vidt gjelder ansvar etter denne para graf svarer den avgiftspliktige for medhjelpe res, ektefelles og barns handlinger. Vedlegg Spørsmål og svar vedrørende forståelsen av avgiftsreglene på enkelte områder innen EF Utvalget har gjennom Finansdepartemen tet, Avgifts- og tollavdelingen, rettet enkelte spørsmål til EF-kommisjonen for å få brakt på det rene hvilke regler som gjelder på be stemte områder. Spørsmålene knytter seg til utvalgets vurdering av konkurransevridning og forslaget til et modifisert avgiftssystem. Spørsmål og svar gjengis nedenfor i sin hehet. QUESTIONNAIRE Concerning Value Added Tax (VAT) I Re: Distortion of competition resulting from activity carried out by non-liable public institutions. Question 1 : Would it be in conformity with Community legislation to make national provisions to the effect that public institutions, whose activiti es are of a wholly non-liable nature, are given right to claim credit for input VAT, borne on acquisitions, thus bringing such institutions into line with liable business enterprises? Comments: A provisions as described above seems to contravene Article 4 No 5 of the Sixth VAT Di rective, which provides that public institu tions are not regarded as liable purposes of VAT when their activity consists of exercising public authority. Hence such public institu tions as referred to seem under Community legislation excluded from claiming registra tion and also from claiming credit for input tax. In the event of an introduction of a regi me as described it is assumed that no loss in a revenue will occur, as the Credit for input VAT will be compensated by a refund over municipal budgets. This compensatory arran gement will also apply in the case of question 2 and 3 below. Question 2: Would it be in conformity with Community legislation to make national provisions which exempt non-liable public institutions from bearing VAT on their acquisitions? Comments: A provisions of this kind would, in effect mean a zero-rating of supplies made to non-li able public institutions. The sixth VAT Direc tive seems to contain no provisions dealing with tax-rates, but signals received regarding the harmonisations of tax rates seem to indi cate that provisions of a nature described, would not conform to proposals made, which proposals go for a linking of tax rates to the kind of the goods and services supplied. Question 3: Would it be in conformity with Community legislation to make national provisions that provides for the application of a reduced basis for calculating VAT when making taxable supplies to non-liable public institutions? Comments: The effect of this alternative is the same as if employing a reduced tak rate, allthough provided in the form of a reduced basis for calculating tax rather than in the form of a re duced rate. Reference is made to comments under question 2. Question 4: Will it be possible to give a survey as to which of the member states apply special me asures to counter act distortion of competi tion between liable entrepreneurs and non-li able public activity, and also if possible, how the actual provisions are formulated? Comments: As the Committee is receiving the Act rela ting to Value-Added Tax, i.a. possible influen ce of VAT on competition between liable en trepreneurs and non-liable public institutions and what measures should be adopted to counter acts distortion of competition, it wold be of help to know the extent to which this has been a problem elsewhere. The Commit tee is well acquainted with relevant legisla tion in Denmark and Sweden. It would be of great interest to be informed of relevant legis lation within the EEC.

side 260

II Re. Modified VAT system Question 5: Would it be in line with the general provi sions in the Community to provide that taxa ble goods and services shall be zero-rated when supplied to entrepreneurs liable to VAT. Svaret lyder slik: QUETIONNAIRE Concerning Value Added Tax (VAT) Question 1 Such a measure would not be compatible with Community Law. Article 4 (5) of the Sixth VAT Directive provides that those acti vities of bodies governed by public law in which they engage as public authorities are, in principle, out of the scope of VAT. To the extent that these bodies are not liable to VAT, they cannot deduct the VAT incurred on their purchases of goods and services. Article 17 (2) of the Sixth VAT Directive limits entitlement to the right of deduction to those goods and services which are used for the purposes of the taxable transactions of a taxable person. Of course, nothing prevents bodies governed by public law from being compensated, with out using the mechanism of VAT, by an amount equal to that of the non-deductible tax. Question 2 The Sixth Directive does not allow the ap plication of a zero rate to the supply of goods and services destined to non-liable bodies go verned by public law. The zero rates which will probably be allowed from 1.1.1993, accor ding to the ECOFIN Council conclusions of 24 june 1991, will have a transitional charac ter, and relate to zero rates already existing in the Member States on 1.1.1991. Furthermore, these zero rates must be for the benefit of fi nal consumers and for well defined social rea sons (Cf. Article 28 (2) of Sixth Directive). Question 3 Article 11 of the Sixth Directive concerning the taxable amount does not provide for the possibility of reducing the taxable amount in this case. Question 4 Question 4 appears to relate to the applica tion of the second paragraph of Article 4 (5) of the Sixth Directive. It is impossible to provi de a complete list of the measures tåken by each Member State on the basis of this provi sion. It is on the basis of a case by case evalua tion that the Member States establish whet her or not there is distortion of competition, and whether the public law body shall be con sidered a taxable person. Provision that a bo dy governed by public law be treated as taxa ble person is often made by means of admini strative provisions relating to the particular case in question. The Commission only has some national regulations, often of a very ge neral character. Attached are copies of some of these regulations which exist in English or French. In all circumstances, however, bodies governed by public law are considered taxa ble persons in relation to the activities of An nex D of the Sixth Directive. Question 5 The principle on which VAT is based is that all supplies of goods and services are taxed which are not specifically exempted. The ap plication of a zero rate in the example that you describe is not permitted by the Sixth Direc tive. The raising of the tax at each stage of the economic cycle, even if there is deduction by the following stage, is made necessary by the VAT mechanism, whose essential objective is the pre-financing of the tax for the benefit of the exchequer. I tilknytning til de eksemplene det er vist til i svaret under punkt 4, gjengis reglene i Storbrittania som følger: Bodies governed by public law [Article 4 (s)] The legal transposition of Article 4 (5) is em bodied in sections 20, 27 and 28 of VAT and re lated Statutory Instruments (see Transposi tion table). In cases where bodies governed by public law engage in activities which are liable to provoke significant distortion of competition these activities are considered as business ac tivities, and the bodies are considered as tax able persons in respect of such activities. Taxable supplies made by the Crown (Go vernment Departments) are treated in the sa me way as taxable supplies made by taxable persons. A government department may eit her supply goods or services as business acti vities, or be deemed to do so by virtue of Trea sury direction. In either case the department, registered for VAT in accordance with the ru les applicable to any other person, is thus en titled to input tax credit in relation to goods and services used or to be used for the purpo ses of its taxable business. Local authorities

with the ru les applicable to any other person, is thus en titled to input tax credit in relation to goods and services used or to be used for the purpo ses of its taxable business. Local authorities

side 261

are liable to registration for VAT whatever the value of their supplies; they are entitled to in put tax credit in relation to its business activi tes as well as those activities it undertakes as a public body. The provisions whereby certain bodies go verned by public law are entitled to a refund from the Treasury of an amount equal to the amount of Value Added Tax incurred by that body in resepct of the activities or transac tions in which they engage as public authori ties are not provided for by Article 4 (5). The UK has always maintained that these are not VAT provisions but national accounting pro visions, and as such are not based on the Sixth Directive. In other words this is not a question og input tax but treasury grants.
